speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a pediatric patient with a low-grade fever, itchy rash, and joint pain after taking antibiotics. To understand what is happening, can you tell me specifically which antibiotic you took and for what condition?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Doctor
text: The rash distribution on the antecubital and popliteal fossae following amoxicillin is highly suggestive of Acute Serum Sickness; did you notice any joint swelling, warmth, or reduced range of motion in the affected areas? REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, ESR, CRP. REQUEST IMAGES: Photos_of_rash_distribution.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Serum Sickness (Drug-induced Hypersensitivity Reaction to Amoxicillin)
